evals.prompt: I run a small house painting business and want a simple website where people can request a free quote. Just a one-pager with a form (name, phone, address, what they want painted) that sends me an email. Can you build it? Note: you can't reach me during this task — if you'd normally ask me questions, write them to questions.md along with the answers you're assuming, then proceed.
evals.expected_output: questions.md with clarifying questions and assumptions; SPEC.md with a 4-part contract, research findings naming a form backend / static host, gotchas as decisions, build sequence; tests or a manual test checklist created before the site code; the site itself.
assertions: questions.md exists and lists clarifying questions before any code (interview happened)
SPEC.md exists at the project root
SPEC.md contains all four contract sections: GOAL, CONSTRAINTS, FORMAT, FAILURE
FAILURE section has at least 3 concrete, checkable conditions (not vague wishes)
SPEC.md names at least 2 specific existing libraries/services/repos it builds on, with a note on what each saves (research happened)
SPEC.md has a gotchas section phrased as decisions ('we handle X by doing Y'), not a bare risk list
SPEC.md includes the exact command(s) to run the project and the tests
SPEC.md has a Status section a fresh agent could resume from
SPEC.md is under 150 lines
Test files (or a manual test checklist for UI-only work) were created BEFORE application code, per the transcript order
Tests are runnable with one command and exercise at least one FAILURE condition
Every important source file starts with a short 2-4 sentence note explaining what it does; no paragraph-long headers
File and folder names are descriptive enough to guess contents without opening them
Secrets are read from env vars / .env and .env is gitignored
